newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MITCHELL'S THREE HITS HELPS ANGELS WIN OVER INDIANS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MITCHELL'S THREE HITS HELPS ANGELS WIN OVER INDIANS.

text.p: Kevin Mitchell had three hits, including his third home run of the season, as the Cleveland Indians used a four-run fifth inning en route to a 7-5 victory over the Anaheim Angels Saturday.

Mitchell led off the fifth with a single off Japanese import Shigetoshi Hasegawa (0-1) and Sandy Alomar hit a 2-1 pitch over the left-field wall for his second homer, pulling the Indians within 4-3. An out later, Omar Vizquel and Jim Thome singled. Matt Williams doubled home Vizquel with the tying run.
"I faced him before over there (in Japan). I pretty much knew what he had," Mitchell said. "He would pretty much try to keep you off-balance."
Chuck McElroy relieved Hasegawa and David Justice's RBI groundout scored Thome to put the Indians ahead for good, 5-4. Justice later homered for Clevenad
Hasegawa, who was making his major-league debut, allowed five runs and seven hits over 4 1/3 innings.

"I had no feeling of fear, I was more concerned with pitching the way I wanted to," Hasegawa said. "In the fourth inning, I started to nit-pick too much on the corners. I was not nervous, I had a lot of positive tension. I was really focused. I'm euphoric about my abilty to play in the big leagues."

"He just started to miss his spots," Anaheim manager Terry Collins said of Hasegawa. "He just got the ball up one too many times. I thought he threw the ball good. When you face a lineup like the Cleveland Indians you have to concentrate the whole game."

Cleveland starter Chad Ogea (1-0) gave up five runs -- three earned -- and seven hits over six innings. Paul Shuey, who surrendered a game-winning grand slam to Tim Salmon on Friday, loaded the bases in the ninth, but did not allow a run and picked up his second save.

In Chicago, Tony Clark hit a pair of solo homers and Bobby Higginson and Damion Easley each hit three-run blasts as the Detroit Tigers outslugged the White Sox 15-12 in the second-longest nine-inning game in major league history.
The game lasted four hours and 20 minutes, one minute shy of the longest nine-inning game, between the Yankees and Orioles on April 30, 1996 at Camden Yards.

The Tigers and White Sox combined for six homers and 31 hits under swirling wind conditions. Clark had four hits and Brian Hunter went 4-for-5 with three RBI and three stolen bases to lead a 19-hit Tiger attack. It was the first career four-hit game and third two-homer game for Clark.
In Oakland, Paul O'Neill capped a six-run third inning with a grand slam and Derek Jeter tied a career high with four hits to lead the New York Yankees past the Athletics, 10-5.
Jose Canseco singled in Oakland's first run in the first inning and belted a two-run homer in the third to make it 6-3. It was his first homer since returning to the Athletics.

Geronimo Berroa and Scott Spiezio hit solo homers in the fourth -- Spiezio's first in the majors -- to get the A's within 6-5, but the Yankees rallied for two more runs in the eighth to keep the lead for Dwight Gooden (1-0).
Gooden allowed five runs and six hits with a walk and three strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings.
In Seattle, Nomar Garciaparra hit a three-run homer off closer Norm Charlton in the top of the ninth, giving the Boston Red Sox a 8-6 victory over the Mariners and spoiling Randy Johnson's return.

Seattle brought a 6-4 lead into the ninth inning. Charlton (0-1), who worked out of an eighth-inning jam, surrendered a leadoff double to former Mariner Bill Haselman and walked Darren Bragg, another former Mariner, before Garciaparra hit a 3-2 pitch just over the scoreboard in right field.
One out later, Mo Vaughn was hit by a pitch and Jeff Frye singled him to third, ending Charlton's night. Josias Manzanillo came on and allowed a sacrifice fly to Tim Naehring, making it 8-6.
Rick Trlicek (1-0) earned his first win in almost exactly three years, allowing an unearned run in two innings. Heathcliff Slocumb pitched the ninth for his second save.
Garciaparra went 2-for-5 with a career-high four RBI. He is 6-for-10 in the series.

Johnson was scratched from his scheduled start on Friday after his infant son was hospitalized with a viral respiratory infection. In his first appearance since last August, the lanky left-hander held Boston to two runs and five hits over six innings with no walks and eight strikeouts.
In Toronto, Gerald Williams homered and doubled in two runs and Jamie McAndrew was a winner in his first appearance since 1995 as the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Blue Jays 5-2.
It was the first win of the season for Milwaukee.
Williams was 0-for-8 this season before belting a two-out homer to centre in the fourth. He got a two-out double in the sixth.

McAndrew (1-0) allowed both runs and seven hits over five innings in his first appearance since suffering a knee injury in August 1995. McAndrew, a replacement player during the player's strike, missed all of 1996 after undergoing surgery.

At Texas, Lenny Webster had three RBI, including a two-run double in a five-run first inning, as the Baltimore Orioles remained the only undefeated team in the majors with a 9-7 victory over the Rangers.
Cal Ripken got his second homer of the season for Baltimore while Lee Stevens and Mickey Tettleton homered for Texas.
At Minnesota, Chuck Knoblauch had three hits and two RBI and Terry Steinbach added two hits and drove in three runs, leading the Twins to a 7-5 win over the Kansas City Royals.
